faqLeft.q: What engine does the Mercedes S65 AMG use?
faqLeft.a: The S65 AMG uses the M275 — a 6.0-litre twin-turbo V12. It was fitted across both the W221 generation (2008–2013) and W222 generation (2013–2020).

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes S65 AMG engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £8,000+, reflecting the very high complexity of the V12. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my S65 AMG?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm your exact engine code and generation before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild M275 S65 AMG engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We rebuild M275 V12s to original specification, replacing timing chains, valve seals, coolant components, and bearings as standard.

faqLeft.q: Do you supply used S65 AMG engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my S65 AMG if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an S65 AMG engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most S65 AMG owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.

faqRight.q: Is the S65 AMG still in production?
faqRight.a: No. The S65 AMG was discontinued after the W222 generation (2020). The V12 role in the current W223 range moved to the Maybach S680. We continue to rebuild and replace engines for every S65 AMG still on the road.
